lead.headline: Sweden's center-left leads by 3 seats as the far right slips
lead.dek: Sweden Democrats lose ground for the first time; late ballots are counted from Wednesday and a final result is due by the end of the week
body: Sweden's center-left opposition held a three-seat lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's governing bloc early Monday with 94% of votes counted, the Swedish Election Authority said, putting Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson in position to form a government after Sunday's parliamentary election.

The opposition was on course for 176 seats in the 349-member Riksdag to 173 for the governing bloc, the authority's preliminary count showed. The Social Democrats led with 28.1% of the vote, down 2.2 points from 2022 and the party's weakest result in more than a century. The far-right Sweden Democrats fell to third, behind the Moderates, the first time the party's share has declined.

Counting of late postal and overseas ballots begins Wednesday, and a final result is expected by the end of the week. Kristersson said he would contact other party leaders once the result is final and that "it's a good idea to look at possible combinations." Andersson said Sweden "will get a new government" if the numbers hold.

briefs.headline: EPA set to repeal power plant carbon limits as soon as today
briefs.summary: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the plan, that the EPA will rescind carbon capture mandates for coal and gas plants at a G20 energy ministers' meeting in Houston.

briefs.headline: Futures put better than 80% odds on a Fed rate hike Wednesday
briefs.summary: The Fed's two-day meeting ends Wednesday with a 2 p.m. ET decision; fed funds futures price better than 80% odds of a quarter-point increase from the 3.5%-3.75% range.

briefs.headline: Lucas Fire containment reaches 25% as winds ease
briefs.summary: The fire near the Lake-Mendocino county line grew to 4,109 acres by Sunday evening with no injuries reported, Cal Fire said; evacuation orders remain in eight zones.

briefs.headline: Gunmen kill 1, wound 6 in Chicago's Humboldt Park
briefs.summary: Shooters in two cars opened fire on a group near an alley on North Christiana Avenue about 12:15 p.m. Sunday, police said; a 14-year-old boy was among the wounded. No arrests.

briefs.headline: Iran and Oman put off Gulf talks on Hormuz shipping
briefs.summary: Oman's foreign minister said Monday's meeting in Salalah was postponed "in the interests of consensus"; Iran's Fars agency said some regional states asked for the delay. No new date was set.

briefs.headline: Search widens for 129 missing in Indonesian ferry sinking
briefs.summary: Six are dead after the Virgo Transport 8 overturned Sunday in the Java Sea; 17 ships and aircraft with 655 personnel searched Monday, Indonesia's rescue agency chief said.

briefs.headline: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop hitting Russian diesel plants
briefs.summary: Speaking in Doonbeg, Ireland, Trump said Sunday the strikes were causing a diesel shortage; Ukraine struck refineries in Krasnodar and Tatarstan the same day.

briefs.headline: Uganda buries Tooro king as family disputes successor
briefs.summary: Oyo Nyimba Rukidi IV, who died of cancer Aug. 27 at 34, was buried Saturday in Fort Portal. Clan elders installed a cousin as king; his family says a 2022 will named a son.

briefs.headline: WVU assistant coach Noel Devine jailed on strangulation charge
briefs.summary: Devine, 38, was booked into North Central Regional Jail on Sunday on a felony strangulation charge with bail set at $40,000, state corrections records show; coach Rich Rodriguez issued a statement Sunday evening.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers open interims with water and flood briefings
briefs.summary: Legislators at the Capitol on Sunday heard the Water Development Authority aims for $1B in water and sewer investment over two years; DEP said federal revolving-fund allotments keep declining.

briefs.headline: PSC staff urges commission to reject $1.16B MARL power line
briefs.summary: Public Service Commission staff said in testimony filed Sept. 8 that the 107.5-mile MidAtlantic Resiliency Link carries no material benefit for West Virginia, joining consumer and landowner advocates opposing it.

regional.item: Huntington City Council votes tonight on a police-technology guardrail ordinance and a $1.58M paving contract with West Virginia Paving.
Two people face animal cruelty charges after officers found dogs in a St. Albans home with no food or water on Friday, court records show.

away.item: The supervisor of a Bennington drug and gun ring was sentenced Sept. 8 in federal court in Rutland to 12 years in prison.

hotspots.item: Holly River State Park's festival and car show drew visitors Sept. 5 and 6 over the Labor Day weekend, The Webster Echo reported Sept. 8.
Topsail Beach said Friday that beach driving, horseback riding and off-leash dogs are no longer allowed on the south-end nature preserve, now state-owned.

briefs.headline: Council backs inland port proposal for Prince George
briefs.summary: City council will give in-principle support to MLA Rosalyn Bird's plan for an armed forces logistics base, a disaster-response training centre and an expanded trade zone at the airport, My PG Now reported Sunday.

briefs.headline: Quesnel walker gets B.C. medal after 700-km healing march
briefs.summary: Archie Chantyman of the Lhoosk'uz Dene Nation finished the March with Arch on Saturday, from Quesnel to the former St. Joseph's Mission at Williams Lake and back, and received the B.C. Medal of Good Citizenship.

briefs.headline: 2 rescued after a fishing vessel sinks off Tsawwassen
briefs.summary: BC Ferries said rescue craft from the Spirit of British Columbia and Coastal Renaissance pulled two boaters from the water Sunday afternoon; later sailings were delayed.

briefs.headline: Alert Bay takes down the world's tallest totem pole
briefs.summary: The Namgis First Nation removed the 173-foot pole, raised in 1973 beside its Big House, after leaders said it could fall on the Big House or on homes across the street.

briefs.headline: Carney opens investment summit with a $1 trillion target
briefs.summary: The prime minister told executives at a Toronto dinner Sunday that deals were already signed ahead of the two-day summit, which seeks $1 trillion in investment over five years.

briefs.headline: Canadian exports to China rise 30% in the first half
briefs.summary: Exports hit $21.74 billion, a first-half record led by an 81.8% jump in energy, a Canada China Business Council and China Institute report said; imports from China fell 5.8%.

briefs.headline: SpaceX flies 700th Falcon, completes SES's O3b mPOWER fleet
briefs.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 2:49 p.m. EDT Sunday with three Boeing-built satellites that complete the 13-spacecraft medium-Earth-orbit constellation; the booster landed at sea on its 29th flight.

briefs.headline: Vega-C to launch Sentinel-3C and FLEX tonight from Kourou
briefs.summary: ESA said flight VV30 is set for 9:21 p.m. EDT from French Guiana. FLEX will measure faint fluorescence from vegetation to track plant health; Sentinel-3C continues Copernicus ocean, land and ice monitoring.

briefs.headline: Pneumococcus subtype shapes air pollution risk, study finds
briefs.summary: Wellcome Sanger Institute researchers analyzed about 59,000 invasive pneumococcal cases over 19 years in South Africa and reported in Nature Microbiology that serotypes 14, 19A and 8 carried the highest risk after pollution exposure.

briefs.headline: NSF shifts grants toward 4 White House-aligned initiatives
briefs.summary: A Sept. 10 letter from acting Director Brian Stone describes a portfolio model mixing investigator-driven grants with NSF-directed calls; staff told Nature the initiatives may draw on $1B the agency holds centrally.

briefs.headline: Trump dismisses calls to slow AI as 'negative forces'
briefs.summary: Speaking in Doonbeg, Ireland, on Sunday, Trump said "whoever wins AI, wins" after Anthropic's Dario Amodei urged labs to pace capability gains; House Speaker Mike Johnson said a moratorium would let China overtake the U.S.

briefs.headline: Gartner tells CIOs AI vendors are 'not enterprise grade'
briefs.summary: Gartner analyst Daryl Plummer said at the firm's symposium in Australia that 86% of CIOs it surveyed see AI risks growing faster than value, and that vendors replace models about every six months without supporting old ones.

weather_ear: Monday's forecast from Jim Claudtore follows at 7:15.
kicker: Only Cabell and Kanawha ran a regional line; the Fed decides Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET, and Vega-C flies tonight at 9:21 p.m. ET.

art.caption: Cardboard voting booths on folding tables in a Swedish school gymnasium on election Sunday, a voter passing between them with ballots.
